egress.terms: Every KVM Slice plan on the vendor page is listed 'Unmetered Bandwidth' and the High Volume plans 'Unlim. 1000 Mbps'; no numeric transfer cap is published on the vendor pages read. No fair-use rule tied to the memory of the slice is stated on the vendor pages read.
egress.free_allowance: unmetered; no numeric transfer cap is published on the vendor pages read

record.interface_detail: block (attach as disk), then sftp/rsync/nfs from the slice
record.tooling: Anything. It is a raw block device on a KVM slice.
record.chaining: Hot-pluggable between slices in the same facility with no reboot, which makes it easy to re-front with a different server. No object API at all ('We may consider an Object Store product down the line, but not at this time').
record.limits_note: Per-object-cap: none. Downgrade impossible. You must order a new slab and migrate. 10 TB hard cap per slab. Requires a base slice, so the true entry cost is a slice plus a slab.

identity_cost.detail: Registration needs a legitimate name and surname and a residential address, placed from a residential ISP; a phone number is not required; payment by PayPal, credit card, cryptocurrency (Coinpayments) or Alipay, with account details matching the payment method.

record.reliability_note: Frantech, operating since 2010, the most consistently recommended block-storage product on LET for a decade. Known friction: signup must come from a residential ISP and is refused from VPN/Tor/datacenter IPs, P.O. boxes rejected. A real obstacle for a privacy-conscious buyer but not an identity-document requirement. Storage is 'enterprise 7200RPM hard drives with an NVME cache and a 40Gbit+ InfiniBand'.

extras.price_verbatim: $5.00/TB/mo flat, plus the base slice. At 5 TB: $25/mo slab + $3.50 slice = $28.50/mo = $5.70/TB all-in. At 20 TB: 2x 10 TB slabs = $100/mo + $3.50 = $103.50/mo = $5.18/TB. The all-in figure is what matters and it is worse than the headline because the slice is mandatory overhead.
